title: Deep learning with TensorFlow and Keras
summary: 36 lessons in TensorFlow and Keras, from tensor arithmetic and gradients to training, neural architectures, diagnosis and a reproducible model release. Compare mechanisms with the paired PyTorch lessons.
north_star: Explain a model computation, prove its training/inference contracts and make only the claims supported by its held-out evidence.

stages.title: From arrays to an auditable update
stages.outcome: Derive and inspect a tiny learning step before relying on a training API.

stages.title: Build, debug and evaluate small networks
stages.outcome: Choose objectives, data pipelines and architectures with explicit information and shape contracts.

stages.title: Reproduce, export and defend a model release
stages.outcome: Prove restart/inference behavior and bound reliability claims with controlled evidence.

lessons.title: A bounded deep-learning investigation
lessons.outcome: Distinguish fitting a function from evidence that it generalizes.
lessons.lab: Inspect a three-point training set and a four-point holdout; write the prediction unit, intended use and forbidden claims before touching a framework.
lessons.verification: Record 3 training points, 4 untouched holdout points and one claim that the tiny exercise cannot establish.

lessons.title: Tensors, axes, dtypes and units
lessons.outcome: Trace each axis and unit through vector arithmetic without accidental broadcasting.
lessons.lab: Use NumPy arrays shaped (3,), (3,1) and (1,3); build a table of addition/multiplication result shapes and label the observation axis.
lessons.verification: The vector/column subtraction produces (3,3); a paired-record subtraction requires equal (3,) shapes. Integer-to-float conversion is explicit.

lessons.title: Linear neurons and matrix contracts
lessons.outcome: Relate a scalar slope to a batched affine layer and verify dimensions.
lessons.lab: Multiply a fixed (2,3) input by a (3,1) weight and add a scalar bias; calculate the first output by hand.

lessons.title: Loss, reduction and what a number measures
lessons.outcome: Compute loss with an explicit example denominator and distinguish it from a metric.
lessons.lab: Compare squared residual sums and means for residuals [1,-1,2], then duplicate the batch and compare both reductions.
lessons.verification: Sum=6 and mean=2; duplication doubles the sum but leaves the mean at 2. Report squared target units.

lessons.title: Derivatives as local sensitivity
lessons.outcome: Check a scalar derivative against a finite difference away from a kink.
lessons.lab: Evaluate f(w)=(w-2)^2 at w=0 with central differences h=0.1,0.01,0.001; contrast absolute slope with a learning step.
lessons.verification: Analytic derivative=-4; all three central differences agree within 1e-10. A derivative is not itself the new parameter.

lessons.title: The chain rule and activation boundaries
lessons.outcome: Explain how local derivatives compose and where a derivative convention matters.
lessons.lab: Trace z=2w, a=z*z, loss=(a-1)^2 at w=1; compare with a ReLU example at a positive value and at zero.
lessons.verification: The polynomial derivative at w=1 is 48 within 1e-8. State that the ReLU kink needs an explicit convention; do not use a finite-difference equality there.

lessons.title: Eager tensors, variables and a tape
lessons.outcome: Identify which forward operations and variables are recorded for differentiation.
lessons.lab: Run scalar Variable examples inside and outside GradientTape; inspect a disconnected gradient and an actual zero gradient.
lessons.verification: For loss=(w-2)^2, gradients at w=0 and w=2 are -4 and 0. A forward result built outside the tape gives None, which is a different observation.

lessons.title: One gradient step you can audit
lessons.outcome: Derive, execute and independently check one SGD update before using a training API.
lessons.lab: Use x=[1,2,3], y=[2,4,6], float64, w=0 and learning rate 0.1; compare an equal-shape target with a mistakenly broadcast column target.
lessons.verification: Correct loss=56/3, gradient=-56/3, updated w=28/15 and new loss=56/675 within 1e-12. The broadcast bug has gradient=-16 despite the same initial loss.

lessons.title: Batches and repeated updates
lessons.outcome: Distinguish examples, batches, epochs and optimizer steps.
lessons.lab: Use six fixed paired records x=[1,2,3,4,5,6], y=2*x and compare batch sizes 1, 2 and 3, logging example IDs and update numbers instead of assuming equal trajectories.
lessons.verification: Six examples with batch size 2 yield 3 updates per epoch; a final short batch is included unless drop_remainder is chosen and documented.

lessons.title: A split is part of the experiment
lessons.outcome: Detect duplicate/group leakage before reporting held-out performance.
lessons.lab: Assign a fixed eight-record fixture with four account IDs to train/validation by account; fit a mean only on train.
lessons.verification: No account ID occurs in both sets. A validation-only extreme changes the all-data mean but not the recorded training normalization.

lessons.title: Keras models and explicit training contracts
lessons.outcome: Map compile/fit/evaluate to the explicit forward-loss-gradient-update sequence.
lessons.lab: Create a one-Dense-unit model with fixed zero initializer; perform exactly one full-batch SGD step on the pilot points with shuffling disabled.
lessons.verification: The zero-bias, no-intercept configuration matches tf-008 within 1e-6 in float32; report dtype and reduction before comparing values.

lessons.title: Capstone: an auditable tiny regressor
lessons.outcome: Present a reproducible training experiment with arithmetic and held-out evidence.
lessons.lab: Build a local three-feature synthetic regression investigation, compare a mean baseline, save the split and explain every update in a tiny diagnostic subset.
lessons.verification: Deliver a clean-run transcript, immutable split IDs, analytic pilot check and separate training/holdout errors; no holdout-driven tuning is allowed.

lessons.title: Binary logits, probabilities and thresholds
lessons.outcome: Use a binary loss with the correct logit/probability convention.
lessons.lab: Compare logits [-2,0,2], sigmoid probabilities and thresholds 0.5 versus 0.8 on fixed labels; deliberately mismatch from_logits.
lessons.verification: At logit 0 the probability is 0.5 and positive-label BCE is log(2) within 1e-6. Threshold changes predictions, not the already fitted logits.

lessons.title: Multiclass and multilabel are different tasks
lessons.outcome: Choose target shape and loss from the task rather than the final layer name.
lessons.lab: Contrast one-of-three integer targets with three independent binary labels; compute cross entropy for uniform three-class logits.
lessons.verification: Uniform three-class CE=log(3); sparse targets are class indices. Multilabel targets have one binary value per class and need independent decisions.

lessons.title: A reproducible tf.data pipeline
lessons.outcome: Keep preprocessing, cardinality and order visible in a bounded dataset pipeline.
lessons.lab: Construct a Dataset from fixed arrays; normalize using only training statistics; batch with a remainder and prefetch 1.
lessons.verification: For five records batched by 2, batch sizes are [2,2,1]. Normalization statistics and IDs are identical after a fresh run; no download/map side effect occurs.

lessons.title: Nonlinearity and initialization
lessons.outcome: Explain why an affine-only network cannot express XOR and inspect a nonlinear construction.
lessons.lab: Use all four XOR inputs; compare an affine threshold with h1=ReLU(x1-x2), h2=ReLU(x2-x1), output=h1+h2 before optional fitting.
lessons.verification: The nonlinear construction produces labels [0,1,1,0] for [(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)]; no affine separator can satisfy all four inequalities.

lessons.title: Regularization and training/evaluation behavior
lessons.outcome: Separate regularization penalties from data loss and switch stochastic layers correctly.
lessons.lab: Compare one fixed weight vector under L1/L2 penalties; call a dropout layer with training=False and training=True.
lessons.verification: For weights [1,-2], L1 sum=3 and L2 squared sum=5. Repeated evaluation calls match; training behavior is tested by invariants, not a cross-platform random bit pattern.

lessons.title: Normalization state and batch dependence
lessons.outcome: Distinguish BatchNorm moving statistics from per-example LayerNorm.
lessons.lab: Use momentum 0.5 and a fixed batch mean [2,4]; inspect the first BatchNorm moving-mean update and compare per-row normalization.
lessons.verification: Starting from zeros, moving mean becomes [1,2]. Evaluation does not update it. Adding an unrelated batch row cannot alter another row under LayerNorm.

lessons.title: Convolution as a local, shared computation
lessons.outcome: Trace a convolution kernel, channels and receptive field on a tiny array.
lessons.lab: Apply kernel [[1,0],[0,-1]] to the fixed 3x3 image containing 1 through 9 with VALID padding and no bias.
lessons.verification: The 2x2 output is all -4. TensorFlow uses cross-correlation convention; rotating the kernel would change this example to +4.

lessons.title: Pooling and augmentation without label leakage
lessons.outcome: Apply only label-preserving training transforms and keep evaluation deterministic.
lessons.lab: Pool a fixed 2x2 patch and horizontally flip a hand-authored image; explain a case where flipping would change the label.
lessons.verification: For [[1,3],[2,4]], max pooling yields 4 and average pooling 2.5. Evaluation receives the original image; unsafe semantic flips are rejected in the data contract.

lessons.title: Sequences, embeddings and padding
lessons.outcome: Carry a padding mask through a small sequence model and loss denominator.
lessons.lab: Use token IDs [2,3,0], where 0 is padding; compare final valid state and masked loss before/after appending padding.
lessons.verification: The valid-token mask is [true,true,false]; two equal log(2) token losses average to log(2), not 2*log(2)/3.

lessons.title: Attention with an explicit information boundary
lessons.outcome: Verify causal masking independently of apparent model accuracy.
lessons.lab: Implement one fixed attention head in TensorFlow and compare its equal-logit result with a NumPy oracle; change only future values.
lessons.verification: Outputs for V=[[2,0],[0,2],[6,6]] are [[2,0],[1,1],[8/3,8/3]] within 1e-6; future changes leave earlier rows unchanged.

lessons.title: Debugging a custom training loop
lessons.outcome: Diagnose a silent missing update and distinguish graph tracing from tensor execution.
lessons.lab: Build a short custom loop with one intentionally disconnected forward value, then repair it and log weights before/after each step.
lessons.verification: The disconnected gradient is None, not zero. The repaired first two pilot updates end at w=448/225 within 1e-12; loss is recomputed after every assignment.

lessons.title: Capstone: a small classifier with honest evaluation
lessons.outcome: Deliver a bounded classifier with a baseline, leakage checks and error analysis.
lessons.lab: Generate local geometric arrays with frozen seeds and group IDs; train at most two small hidden layers and compare a simple baseline on an untouched test split.
lessons.verification: Report confusion counts summing to the test cardinality, per-group errors, training-only preprocessing and the chosen validation decision. No promised accuracy threshold substitutes for these checks.

lessons.title: Embedding objectives and negative examples
lessons.outcome: Connect embedding similarity to the objective and negative sampling policy.
lessons.lab: Use a=[1,0], positive=[1,1] and negative=[0,1]; calculate dot products and cosines, then replace the negative with a duplicate of the positive.
lessons.verification: Dot products are 1 and 0; cosine similarities are 1/sqrt(2) and 0. A negative identical to the positive is flagged before a contrastive loss is interpreted.

lessons.title: Custom layers, residuals and trainable state
lessons.outcome: Create weights once and keep build/call responsibilities separate.
lessons.lab: Implement a tiny residual layer, call it twice with the same feature dimension and inspect its tracked variables.
lessons.verification: Variable count does not grow on the second call. A residual addition requires matching trailing dimensions; incompatible inputs produce a declared validation failure.

lessons.title: Transfer learning without a model download
lessons.outcome: Freeze and adapt a locally trained feature extractor with an explicit gradient boundary.
lessons.lab: Reuse the small classifier from tf-024, freeze its base, train a new head for a relabeled local task and compare gradient/weight changes.
lessons.verification: Frozen-base weights remain byte-identical while at least one head weight changes; an unfreeze phase uses a new, declared optimizer policy.

lessons.title: Restartable training and checkpoint evidence
lessons.outcome: Prove a checkpoint restores the next update rather than only the current predictions.
lessons.lab: Train a tiny model for two Adam updates with dropout disabled; save model and optimizer state, restore in a fresh process and compare the next update on the identical batch.
lessons.verification: Uninterrupted and restored next-step weights agree within declared 1e-6 float32 tolerance. A weights-only restart intentionally exposes missing optimizer state.

lessons.title: Precision, overflow and stable objectives
lessons.outcome: Locate overflow before it becomes a misleading training conclusion.
lessons.lab: Compare naive exp/log cross entropy with a stable logits-based form at logits [1000,999]; inspect finite values and gradients.
lessons.verification: The naive exponential path overflows; the stable positive-first-class loss is log(1+exp(-1)) within 1e-6. Mixed precision is an optional hardware study, not a default speed claim.

lessons.title: Distributed gradient semantics on one CPU
lessons.outcome: Distinguish a mean over examples from an unweighted mean over unequal shards.
lessons.lab: Simulate shards of sizes 1 and 3 with fixed gradients; compare naive shard averaging with example-weighted aggregation and gradient accumulation.
lessons.verification: Shard means 2 and 6 combine to 5 when weighted 1:3, not 4. A microbatch accumulator matches the full-batch mean before any optional distributed runtime.

lessons.title: Graphs, retracing and measurement
lessons.outcome: Separate trace/setup cost from steady-state execution and preserve equivalent results.
lessons.lab: Wrap the stateless tensor function f(x)=x*x+1 with tf.function; record tracing counts for repeated float32 signatures and a float64 signature, then measure warmup separately.
lessons.verification: For x=[1,2], both eager and graph outputs are [2,5]. Repeated equal signatures reuse a trace; changed dtype is reported separately. No universal speedup is asserted.

lessons.title: Saving, export and inference parity
lessons.outcome: Choose the correct Keras 3 save/export API and verify a restored prediction contract.
lessons.lab: Save a tiny model as .keras, export an inference artifact with model.export, and compare fixed inputs in a fresh process.
lessons.verification: Both restored paths match the reference predictions within 1e-6. Keras 3 model.save(directory) is not presented as a SavedModel export workflow.

lessons.title: Inference contracts and bounded batching
lessons.outcome: Validate an inference request independently of training success.
lessons.lab: Implement a local predict function with shape, dtype, finite-value and maximum-batch checks; no web server or deployment is started.
lessons.verification: Batch 1 and batched predictions agree per record; empty, nonfinite and over-limit inputs produce named validation errors rather than silent coercion.

lessons.title: Robustness, privacy and model evidence
lessons.outcome: Bound a reliability or privacy claim to the observations actually collected.
lessons.lab: Build an error table over fixed perturbations, rare groups and a duplicate-data counterexample; draft a model card for the tiny classifier.
lessons.verification: The report names the evaluation unit, each tested group, sample count and untested conditions. It makes no differential-privacy or production-safety claim from a small red-team set.

lessons.title: Comparing models with uncertainty
lessons.outcome: Use paired evidence and keep model selection separate from final assessment.
lessons.lab: Compare two saved prediction vectors on the same held-out IDs; use a seeded paired resampling calculation and trace which decisions consumed validation data.
lessons.verification: Paired differences are keyed by the same IDs, bootstrap samples preserve pairs, and no test result is used to choose a new configuration.

lessons.title: Capstone: release a small, reproducible model
lessons.outcome: Defend a local model release with reproducibility, inference and rollback evidence.
lessons.lab: Package the tiny trained model, preprocessing schema, split hashes and next-step checkpoint proof; run a fresh-process prediction contract and a deliberately failing release check.
lessons.verification: Acceptance requires all deterministic contract checks, frozen-test evidence, limitations and a rollback artifact. A failed schema or hash blocks the release recommendation.

capstones.title: An auditable tiny regressor
capstones.brief: Build a tiny regression experiment with an independent arithmetic oracle.
deliverables: baseline comparison and an error explanation
acceptance: The tf-008 oracle matches within its stated tolerance.
Training statistics use training IDs only.
Held-out results are reported separately and never used for another tuning decision.

capstones.title: A small classifier with honest evaluation
capstones.brief: Compare a small local classifier with a transparent baseline.
deliverables: failure case and a revision justified on validation only
acceptance: Model has at most two hidden layers and uses only local fixtures.
Confusion counts sum to test cardinality and groups remain disjoint.
A weak model is reported honestly; no arbitrary accuracy target conceals errors.

capstones.title: A reproducible local model release
capstones.brief: Assemble a release decision from training, inference, provenance and rollback evidence.
deliverables: model card, release decision and rollback artifact
acceptance: Fresh predictions agree within declared tolerance.
Optimizer-state restoration reproduces the next step.
The model card separates tested behavior, untested conditions and intended use.

pilot.code:
import math
import tensorflow as tf

# A CPU-only arithmetic experiment, not a model-quality benchmark.
with tf.device("/CPU:0"):
    x = tf.constant([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], dtype=tf.float64)
    y = tf.constant([2.0, 4.0, 6.0], dtype=tf.float64)
    w = tf.Variable(0.0, dtype=tf.float64)
    learning_rate = tf.constant(0.1, dtype=tf.float64)

    with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
        prediction = w * x
        loss = tf.reduce_mean(tf.square(prediction - y))
    gradient = tape.gradient(loss, w)
    if gradient is None:
        raise ValueError("The loss is disconnected from w")
    before = float(loss.numpy())
    grad = float(gradient.numpy())
    w.assign_sub(learning_rate * gradient)
    after = float(tf.reduce_mean(tf.square(w * x - y)).numpy())

assert math.isclose(before, 56 / 3, rel_tol=0, abs_tol=1e-12)
assert math.isclose(grad, -56 / 3, rel_tol=0, abs_tol=1e-12)
assert math.isclose(float(w.numpy()), 28 / 15, rel_tol=0, abs_tol=1e-12)
assert math.isclose(after, 56 / 675, rel_tol=0, abs_tol=1e-12)
print({"loss_before": before, "gradient": grad,
       "weight_after": float(w.numpy()), "loss_after": after})

concept.title: One learning step is an inspectable state transition
concept.explanation: The forward computation produces a mean squared loss. GradientTape records how that loss depends on the scalar Variable w. The gradient is sensitivity at the old w; assign_sub applies a separate state update. Recompute loss after the update. Equal observation shapes are part of the mathematical contract.
concept.worked_example: For x=[1,2,3], y=2x and w=0, L=56/3 and dL/dw=-56/3. With learning rate 0.1, w becomes 28/15 and the recomputed loss becomes 56/675. Use float64 and absolute tolerance 1e-12.

prediction.prompt: Before running the fixed three-point example, which gradient and update should you expect?
choices: The gradient is -56/3 and w becomes 28/15.
The gradient is +56/3 and w becomes -28/15.
The gradient is None because x is a constant tensor.
prediction.explanation: The tape follows operations from watched Variable w to the loss. The gradient is negative at w=0, so subtracting it increases w toward 2; x does not have to be trainable.

hint_steps: Write the three residuals at w=0, square them and divide their sum by 3.
Differentiate each residual square with respect to w; keep the same denominator 3 and inspect whether every forward operation is inside the tape.
The new weight is old_weight minus learning_rate times gradient. Check shapes before interpreting a matching scalar loss.
pilot.transfer_prompt: Add a scalar bias for targets y=2x+1. Derive both gradients and inspect one held-out prediction without tuning on that held-out point.
rubric: State tensor shapes, float64 dtype, loss reduction and units.
Match the independent loss/gradient/update oracle within 1e-12.
Distinguish None, a legitimate zero gradient and an overly large step.
Detect a broadcasting bug even when initial scalar losses agree.
Separate arithmetic correctness and training loss from held-out or production-quality claims.
